bug_semantics: The authenticated PUT /user/{id} flow accepted a full JSON user object, copied its client-controlled IsAdmin boolean into the domain.User, and allowed a non-admin to update their own identifier. UpdateUser preserved only BaseModel and LinkedPeerCount before saving, so it did not restore the stored IsAdmin value. A non-admin could therefore submit IsAdmin=true for their own account, persist administrator status, and obtain an administrator session after reauthentication.
flaw_origin: The public mainline commit 8b820a5adf119f50757e0236ac98e842eedd35db is a squash of PR #172. Decomposing that squash through the public 41-commit PR patch identifies its first member, 94f0b26304e073d377deaeaaac8b8c6ab967e5e5 (Start Github V2 branch), as the atomic public commit that introduced the vulnerable v2 user-update mechanism: the self-update handler and route, JSON IsAdmin field and NewDomainUser assignment, UpdateUser save path, and CopyCalculatedAttributes implementation that omitted IsAdmin. Its direct parent 3c2c7f325b9741cf168029b12287703400e87269 lacks those v2 paths and the vulnerable mechanism.
ai_marker: absent: BIC 94f0b26304e073d377deaeaaac8b8c6ab967e5e5 has human author Christoph Haas <christoph.h@sprinternet.at>, human committer h44z/Christoph Haas, subject 'Start Github V2 branch', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer in the commit message
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-5rmx-256w-8mj9 and the CVE.org API record for CVE-2026-27899 describe the same privilege-escalation mechanism, list versions before 2.1.3 as affected, and identify v2.1.3 as patched; the CVE record state is PUBLISHED, not rejected or withdrawn.

At vulnerable tag v2.1.2 (6e47d8c3e91a83bfdae10f97b740a22d247fb847), internal/app/api/v0/handlers/endpoint_users.go decodes the PUT body into model.User and passes model.NewDomainUser(&user) to UpdateUser; internal/app/api/v0/model/models_user.go exposes IsAdmin as json:"IsAdmin" and copies src.IsAdmin into domain.User.

At v2.1.2, internal/app/users/user_manager.go permits an authenticated user to update their own identifier, then calls user.CopyCalculatedAttributes(existingUser) and saves; internal/domain/user.go CopyCalculatedAttributes copies only BaseModel and LinkedPeerCount, leaving the request-controlled IsAdmin unchanged.

git blame at v2.1.2 attributes the vulnerable handler, model IsAdmin binding, NewDomainUser IsAdmin assignment, UpdateUser save path, and incomplete CopyCalculatedAttributes implementation to squash commit 8b820a5adf119f50757e0236ac98e842eedd35db.

https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/h44z/wg-portal/pull/172.patch contains 41 member commits; patch 01/41 is 94f0b26304e073d377deaeaaac8b8c6ab967e5e5 and adds the vulnerable files and lines in internal/ports/api/v0/handlers/endpoint_users.go, internal/ports/api/v0/model/models_user.go, internal/app/user.go, and internal/domain/user.go. Later members move/refactor the same mechanism but do not first introduce it.

The GitHub commit page for 94f0b26304e073d377deaeaaac8b8c6ab967e5e5 identifies direct parent 3c2c7f325b9741cf168029b12287703400e87269. git cat-file confirms that parent object locally; git ls-tree shows none of the new v2 user handler/model/domain paths, while its old internal/server/handlers_user.go update path is an administrator form path rather than an authenticated self-update endpoint. This directly verifies parent absence.

The BIC commit page and .patch show authoredDate and committedDate 2023-02-12T23:13:04+01:00, author h44z/Christoph Haas, committer h44z/Christoph Haas, subject 'Start Github V2 branch', and no commit-message AI, bot, Co-Authored-By, or generated-code marker.

Squash commit 8b820a5adf119f50757e0236ac98e842eedd35db contains the reconstructed BIC and is an ancestor of v2.0.0-alpha.1, v2.0.0, vulnerable v2.1.2, and patched v2.1.3, placing the flaw before every affected v2 release boundary checked.

git show fe4485037a25426446ced95050e9498f477bf71d shows the direct fix: non-admin UpdateUser requests have CopyAdminAttributes restore stored IsAdmin and other protected fields, and validateAdminModifications rejects new.IsAdmin for a non-admin. The fix's sole parent is vulnerable tag commit 6e47d8c3e91a83bfdae10f97b740a22d247fb847 (v2.1.2).
Tag v2.1.3 resolves to 0a8ec71b3fb289992a1f00bfebce2145007695ee and contains fe4485037a25426446ced95050e9498f477bf71d; v2.1.2 does not contain the fix, matching the advisory's patched boundary.
reasoning: This is a real authorization vulnerability, not an advisory false positive: both the published CVE record and the vulnerable v2.1.2 tree establish a source-to-sink path from attacker-controlled JSON IsAdmin through model conversion to database save. The smallest reconstructable public BIC is PR member 94f0b26304e073d377deaeaaac8b8c6ab967e5e5, not its later mainline squash 8b820a5adf119f50757e0236ac98e842eedd35db: member 94f0b263 simultaneously creates the vulnerable v2 endpoint/model/save mechanism, and its immediate parent 3c2c7f325b9741cf168029b12287703400e87269 lacks that mechanism. The member was reconstructed from PR #172's public patch series, and later members only refactor or move the already-vulnerable flow. The direct fix fe4485037a25426446ced95050e9498f477bf71d is immediately after v2.1.2 and is contained in v2.1.3, so release topology agrees with the affected and patched ranges. Finally, BIC-only attribution finds a human author and committer and no AI marker or trailer on 94f0b263; the squash's Co-authored-by trailer is not used to attribute the BIC. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
